chapters.title: The Fear of the LORD Is the Beginning of Knowledge
chapters.html:
Proverbs 1

1The proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel:

2for knowing wisdom and discipline,
for understanding words of insight,

3for receiving the discipline of wise dealing,
righteousness, justice and equity;

4to give shrewdness to the simple,
knowledge and discretion to the young —

5let the wise hear and increase in learning,
and the one who understands gain guidance —

6to understand a proverb and a figure,
the words of the wise and their riddles.

7The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge;
fools despise wisdom and discipline.

8Hear, my son, your father's discipline,
and do not forsake your mother's teaching;

9for they are a graceful garland for your head
and pendants for your neck.

10My son, if sinners entice you,
do not consent.

11If they say, "Come with us;
let us lie in wait for blood;
let us ambush the innocent without cause;

12let us swallow them alive like Sheol,
whole, like those who go down to the pit;

13we will find all kinds of precious wealth;
we will fill our houses with plunder;

14cast your lot among us;
we will all have one purse" —

15my son, do not walk in the way with them;
hold back your foot from their path,

16for their feet run to evil,
and they hurry to shed blood.

17For in vain is a net spread
in the sight of any bird;

18but these men lie in wait for their own blood;
they ambush their own lives.

19Such are the ways of everyone who is greedy for gain;
it takes away the life of its owners.

20Wisdom cries aloud in the street;
in the squares she raises her voice;

21at the head of the noisy streets she calls out;
at the entrances of the city gates she speaks her words:

22"How long, you simple ones, will you love being simple?
How long will scoffers delight in their scoffing
and fools hate knowledge?

23Turn back at my reproof;
I will pour out my spirit to you;
I will make my words known to you.

24Because I called and you refused,
I stretched out my hand and no one paid attention,

25because you ignored all my counsel
and would have none of my reproof,

26I also will laugh at your calamity;
I will mock when terror comes on you,

27when terror comes on you like a storm
and your calamity comes like a whirlwind,
when distress and anguish come upon you.

28Then they will call on me, but I will not answer;
they will seek me diligently but will not find me,

29because they hated knowledge
and did not choose the fear of the LORD,

30would have none of my counsel,
and despised all my reproof.

31So they will eat the fruit of their way
and be filled with their own schemes.

32For the turning away of the simple will kill them,
and the complacency of fools will destroy them;

33but whoever listens to me will dwell secure
and be at ease, without dread of evil."

Notes

  • v1 "The proverbs of Solomon" — mishlei, sayings that compare one thing with another; the title of the whole book (1 Kings 4:32, he spoke three thousand proverbs). In the Ethiopian Bible, Proverbs is chapters 1–24; chapters 25–31 form the book called Reproof (Tegsat).

  • vv2–6 and the words for wisdom — each keeps one English word through the book: chokhmah "wisdom," musar "discipline," binah "understanding" or "insight," da'at "knowledge," ormah "shrewdness," mezimmah "discretion," peti "simple," lets "scoffer." Two words are both "fool": evil (v7), the morally foolish, and kesil (v22), the dull and stubborn.

  • v7 "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge" — the motto of the book; 9:10 and Psalm 111:10 have "wisdom."

  • v8 "your mother's teaching" — torah, "law" when it is God's (Psalm 119), here a parent's teaching in the home.

  • v12 "whole" — temimim, elsewhere "blameless" in this rendering; here, set beside "alive," it means whole, swallowed entire.

  • vv17–18 "in vain is a net spread in the sight of any bird" — a bird that sees the net avoids it; these men walk into their own trap with their eyes open.

  • vv20–33 — Wisdom speaks as a woman in the public square, like a prophet calling the city to turn (Jeremiah 7:13; Isaiah 65:12).

  • v23 "I will pour out my spirit to you" — Wisdom's own spirit, lowercase; compare Joel 2:28, where it is God's.

  • v27 "like a storm" — the read form; the written form is a spelling variant.

chapters.title: If You Seek It Like Silver
chapters.html:
Proverbs 2

1My son, if you receive my words
and treasure up my commandments with you,

2making your ear attentive to wisdom
and inclining your heart to understanding;

3yes, if you call out for insight
and raise your voice for understanding,

4if you seek it like silver
and search for it as for hidden treasures,

5then you will understand the fear of the LORD
and find the knowledge of God.

6For the LORD gives wisdom;
from His mouth come knowledge and understanding.

7He stores up sound wisdom for the upright;
He is a shield to those who walk in integrity,

8guarding the paths of justice
and watching over the way of His faithful ones.

9Then you will understand righteousness and justice
and equity, every good path;

10for wisdom will come into your heart,
and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul;

11discretion will watch over you;
understanding will guard you,

12to deliver you from the way of evil,
from men who speak perverse things,

13who forsake the paths of uprightness
to walk in the ways of darkness,

14who rejoice in doing evil
and delight in the perversity of evil,

15whose paths are crooked
and who are devious in their ways.

16It will deliver you from the strange woman,
from the foreign woman with her smooth words,

17who forsakes the companion of her youth
and forgets the covenant of her God;

18for her house sinks down to death,
and her paths to the shades;

19none who go to her come back,
nor do they reach the paths of life.

20So you will walk in the way of the good
and keep to the paths of the righteous.

21For the upright will dwell in the land,
and the blameless will remain in it;

22but the wicked will be cut off from the land,
and the treacherous will be uprooted from it.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "if… if… if" — one long sentence: the seeking is the son's, and the gift is God's (v6).

  • v7 "He stores up" — the read form; the written form has "and He stored up." "Sound wisdom" is tushiyyah, practical skill that succeeds.

  • v8 "His faithful ones" — the read form, plural; the written form is singular. Chasid, as in the Psalms.

  • v16 "the strange woman… the foreign woman" — zarah and nokhriyyah: another man's wife, outside the bounds of the marriage covenant, the figure of chapters 5–7.

  • v17 "the covenant of her God" — marriage as a covenant made before God (Malachi 2:14).

  • v18 "the shades" — refa'im, the dead (Psalm 88:10).

  • vv21–22 — the land kept by the upright and lost by the wicked, as in Psalm 37:9–11, 29.

chapters.title: Trust in the LORD with All Your Heart
chapters.html:
Proverbs 3

1My son, do not forget my teaching,
but let your heart keep my commandments,

2for length of days and years of life
and peace they will add to you.

3Do not let loyal love and truth forsake you;
bind them around your neck;
write them on the tablet of your heart.

4So you will find favor and good understanding
in the sight of God and man.

5Trust in the LORD with all your heart,
and do not lean on your own understanding.

6In all your ways acknowledge Him,
and He will make your paths straight.

7Do not be wise in your own eyes;
fear the LORD and turn away from evil.

8It will be healing to your navel
and refreshment to your bones.

9Honor the LORD with your wealth
and with the firstfruits of all your produce;

10then your barns will be filled with plenty,
and your vats will burst with new wine.

11My son, do not reject the discipline of the LORD,
and do not resent His reproof,

12for the LORD reproves the one He loves,
as a father the son in whom he delights.

13Blessed is the one who finds wisdom,
and the one who gains understanding,

14for her profit is better than profit from silver,
and her yield than fine gold.

15She is more precious than jewels,
and nothing you desire can compare with her.

16Long life is in her right hand;
in her left hand are riches and honor.

17Her ways are ways of pleasantness,
and all her paths are peace.

18She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her,
and those who hold her fast are called blessed.

19The LORD by wisdom founded the earth;
by understanding He established the heavens;

20by His knowledge the deeps broke open,
and the clouds drop down the dew.

21My son, do not let them slip from your sight;
keep sound wisdom and discretion,

22and they will be life for your soul
and grace for your neck.

23Then you will walk your way in safety,
and your foot will not stumble.

24When you lie down, you will not be afraid;
when you lie down, your sleep will be sweet.

25Do not be afraid of sudden terror
or of the ruin of the wicked when it comes,

26for the LORD will be your confidence
and will keep your foot from being caught.

27Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due,
when it is in your power to do it.

28Do not say to your neighbor, "Go, and come back;
tomorrow I will give it" —
when you have it with you.

29Do not plot harm against your neighbor,
who lives trustingly beside you.

30Do not quarrel with anyone without cause,
when he has done you no harm.

31Do not envy a man of violence,
and do not choose any of his ways,

32for the devious person is detestable to the LORD,
but His confidence is with the upright.

33The LORD's curse is on the house of the wicked,
but He blesses the dwelling of the righteous.

34Toward the scoffers He is scornful,
but to the humble He gives grace.

35The wise will inherit honor,
but fools carry away disgrace.

Notes

  • v3 "loyal love and truth… write them on the tablet of your heart" — chesed and emet, as in Exodus 34:6; the tablet as in Jeremiah 31:33.

  • v8 "healing to your navel" — shor, the navel or the cord; the Greek reads "your body."

  • v11 "do not resent His reproof" — qots, to dread or recoil from; "loathe" is kept in this rendering for sheqets.

  • vv11–12 — Hebrews 12:5–6 quotes these lines from the Greek, which reads the last line "and He scourges every son whom He receives."

  • v15 "more precious than jewels" — peninim, perhaps corals or pearls; the read form is a spelling variant.

  • v18 "a tree of life" — as in Genesis 2:9 and 3:22; wisdom gives what was lost (Revelation 22:2).

  • vv19–20 — the same wisdom by which God made the world, as in 8:22–31 and Psalm 104:24.

  • vv27–28 — "to whom it is due" and "your neighbor" are the read forms; the written forms are spelling variants.

  • v34 "to the humble He gives grace" — the read form anavim, "humble"; the written form aniyyim, "afflicted." James 4:6 and 1 Peter 5:5 quote the Greek: God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.

chapters.title: Keep Your Heart
chapters.html:
Proverbs 4

1Hear, sons, a father's discipline,
and pay attention, so that you may know understanding,

2for I give you good learning;
do not forsake my teaching.

3When I was a son to my father,
tender, the only one in the sight of my mother,

4he taught me and said to me,
"Let your heart hold fast my words;
keep my commandments and live.

5Get wisdom; get understanding;
do not forget, and do not turn away from the words of my mouth.

6Do not forsake her, and she will keep you;
love her, and she will guard you.

7The beginning of wisdom is this: get wisdom,
and with all you have gotten, get understanding.

8Prize her highly, and she will exalt you;
she will honor you if you embrace her.

9She will place on your head a graceful garland;
she will give you a crown of beauty."

10Hear, my son, and accept my words,
and the years of your life will be many.

11I have taught you the way of wisdom;
I have led you in paths of uprightness.

12When you walk, your step will not be hampered,
and if you run, you will not stumble.

13Keep hold of discipline; do not let go;
guard her, for she is your life.

14Do not enter the path of the wicked,
and do not walk in the way of evil men.

15Avoid it; do not go on it;
turn away from it and pass on.

16For they cannot sleep unless they have done evil;
they are robbed of sleep unless they have made someone stumble.

17For they eat the bread of wickedness
and drink the wine of violence.

18But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn,
which shines brighter and brighter until full day.

19The way of the wicked is like deep darkness;
they do not know what makes them stumble.

20My son, pay attention to my words;
incline your ear to my sayings.

21Do not let them slip from your sight;
keep them within your heart.

22For they are life to those who find them,
and healing to all their flesh.

23Above all that you guard, keep your heart,
for from it flow the springs of life.

24Put away from you crooked speech,
and put devious lips far from you.

25Let your eyes look straight ahead,
and your gaze be fixed straight before you.

26Make level the path of your feet,
and all your ways will be sure.

27Do not turn to the right or to the left;
turn your foot away from evil.

Notes

  • vv3–9 — the father passes on what his own father taught him: three generations of the same teaching.

  • v3 "the only one in the sight of my mother" — yachid, an only or beloved son; Solomon was the son David and Bathsheba kept (2 Samuel 12:24).

  • v7 "The beginning of wisdom is this: get wisdom" — the first step is the decision to seek it, whatever it costs; the Greek leaves out the verse.

  • v16 "unless they have made someone stumble" — the read form; the written form is a spelling variant.

  • v18 "like the light of dawn, which shines brighter and brighter" — the righteous grow in light; the wicked walk in darkness and do not even see what trips them (v19).

  • v20 "my sayings" — amarai, the plural of imrah; here the father's spoken words.

  • v23 "Above all that you guard, keep your heart" — the heart, the seat of thought and will, from which life flows (Matthew 15:18–19).

chapters.title: Drink Water from Your Own Cistern
chapters.html:
Proverbs 5

1My son, pay attention to my wisdom;
incline your ear to my understanding,

2so that you may keep discretion
and your lips may guard knowledge.

3For the lips of the strange woman drip honey,
and her mouth is smoother than oil;

4but in the end she is bitter as wormwood,
sharp as a two-edged sword.

5Her feet go down to death;
her steps take hold of Sheol.

6She does not consider the path of life;
her ways wander, and she does not know it.

7Now then, sons, listen to me,
and do not turn away from the words of my mouth.

8Keep your way far from her,
and do not go near the door of her house,

9or you will give your vigor to others
and your years to the merciless,

10or strangers will take their fill of your strength,
and your labors will go to the house of a foreigner,

11and at the end of your life you will groan,
when your flesh and body are consumed,

12and you will say, "How I hated discipline,
and my heart despised reproof!

13I did not listen to the voice of my teachers
or incline my ear to my instructors.

14I was almost in utter ruin
in the assembly and congregation."

15Drink water from your own cistern,
flowing water from your own well.

16Should your springs be scattered abroad,
streams of water in the streets?

17Let them be yours alone,
and not for strangers with you.

18Let your fountain be blessed,
and rejoice in the wife of your youth,

19a loving doe, a graceful mountain goat.
Let her breasts satisfy you at all times;
be captivated always by her love.

20Why, my son, should you be captivated by a strange woman
and embrace the bosom of a foreigner?

21For a man's ways are before the eyes of the LORD,
and He weighs all his paths.

22The iniquities of the wicked man ensnare him,
and he is held fast in the cords of his sin.

23He dies for lack of discipline,
and in the greatness of his folly he goes astray.

Notes

  • v3 "the strange woman" — zarah, as in 2:16, another man's wife.

  • v6 "She does not consider the path of life" — pen, often "lest," here "so that she does not": she never stops to weigh her way.

  • vv9–10 "or you will give… or strangers will take" — pen, "or else": adultery costs strength, years and wealth.

  • v14 "in the assembly and congregation" — exposed and judged before the whole community (Deuteronomy 22:22).

  • vv15–18 "cistern… well… springs… fountain" — the wife as the man's own well of water (Song of Songs 4:12, 15); v16 can be read as a question or as a statement of a blessing that spreads to children.

  • vv19, 20, 23 "be captivated… be captivated… goes astray" — the same verb, shagah, three times: be lost in your wife's love, not in a stranger's, or you will be lost in your folly.

  • v21 "He weighs all his paths" — or "levels"; God sees and measures every way.

chapters.title: Go to the Ant, You Sluggard
chapters.html:
Proverbs 6

1My son, if you have become surety for your neighbor,
have given your pledge for a stranger,

2you are snared by the words of your mouth,
caught by the words of your mouth.

3Do this, then, my son, and save yourself,
since you have come into your neighbor's hand:
go, humble yourself, and press your neighbor hard.

4Give no sleep to your eyes
or slumber to your eyelids;

5save yourself like a gazelle from the hunter's hand,
like a bird from the hand of the fowler.

6Go to the ant, you sluggard;
consider her ways and be wise.

7She has no chief,
officer or ruler,

8yet she prepares her bread in summer
and gathers her food at harvest.

9How long will you lie there, sluggard?
When will you rise from your sleep?

10A little sleep, a little slumber,
a little folding of the hands to rest,

11and your poverty will come on you like a prowler,
and your want like an armed man.

12A worthless person, a wicked man,
goes about with crooked speech,

13winks with his eyes, signals with his feet,
points with his fingers,

14with perversity in his heart devises evil continually,
sowing discord.

15So calamity will come on him suddenly;
in an instant he will be broken beyond healing.

16There are six things the LORD hates,
seven that are detestable to Him:

17haughty eyes, a lying tongue,
and hands that shed innocent blood,

18a heart that devises wicked plans,
feet that hurry to run to evil,

19a false witness who breathes out lies,
and one who sows discord among brothers.

20My son, keep your father's commandment,
and do not forsake your mother's teaching.

21Bind them on your heart always;
tie them around your neck.

22When you walk, it will lead you;
when you lie down, it will watch over you;
and when you awake, it will talk with you.

23For the commandment is a lamp and the teaching a light,
and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life,

24to keep you from the evil woman,
from the smooth tongue of the foreign woman.

25Do not desire her beauty in your heart,
and do not let her capture you with her eyelashes;

26for a prostitute costs only a loaf of bread,
but another man's wife hunts for a precious life.

27Can a man carry fire in his lap
and his clothes not be burned?

28Or can a man walk on hot coals
and his feet not be scorched?

29So is he who goes in to his neighbor's wife;
none who touches her will go unpunished.

30People do not despise a thief if he steals
to satisfy his hunger when he is hungry;

31yet if he is caught, he will pay sevenfold;
he will give all the goods of his house.

32He who commits adultery with a woman lacks sense;
he who does it destroys himself.

33He will get wounds and disgrace,
and his reproach will not be wiped away.

34For jealousy makes a man furious,
and he will not spare in the day of vengeance.

35He will accept no compensation;
he will refuse, though you multiply gifts.

  • v1 "if you have become surety" — guaranteeing another's debt with a handshake (taqa kaf, "struck hands"); the book warns against it again (11:15; 17:18; 22:26–27).

  • v6 "Go to the ant, you sluggard" — atsel, the lazy man, a figure the book returns to (24:30–34 repeats vv10–11).

  • v14 "sowing discord" — the read form midyanim; the written form is a spelling variant.

  • v16 "six things… seven" — the numerical saying, the last item the one that matters most (30:15–31; Amos 1:3). "Detestable" is to'evah; the read form is singular.

  • v23 "the commandment is a lamp and the teaching a light" — as in Psalm 119:105.

  • v26 "a prostitute costs only a loaf of bread" — the Hebrew is terse, "for a prostitute — to a loaf of bread"; the cost of the one is small, of the other a life.

  • v32 "lacks sense" — chasar lev, literally "lacks heart," the heart as the seat of understanding.

  • vv34–35 — the wronged husband's jealousy, which no payment will buy off; the thief can repay (v31), the adulterer cannot.

chapters.title: Her House Is the Way to Sheol
chapters.html:
Proverbs 7

1My son, keep my words
and treasure up my commandments with you.

2Keep my commandments and live;
keep my teaching as the apple of your eye.

3Bind them on your fingers;
write them on the tablet of your heart.

4Say to wisdom, "You are my sister,"
and call understanding your close relative,

5to keep you from the strange woman,
from the foreign woman with her smooth words.

6For at the window of my house
I looked out through my lattice,

7and I saw among the simple,
I noticed among the youths,
a young man lacking sense,

8passing along the street near her corner,
taking the road to her house

9in the twilight, in the evening of the day,
in the black of night and the darkness.

10Then a woman comes to meet him,
dressed as a prostitute, with a guarded heart.

11She is loud and unruly;
her feet do not stay at home;

12now in the street, now in the squares,
and at every corner she lies in wait.

13She seizes him and kisses him,
and with a brazen face she says to him,

14"I had peace offerings to make;
today I have paid my vows.

15So I came out to meet you,
to seek your face eagerly, and I have found you.

16I have spread my bed with coverings,
colored linens from Egypt.

17I have sprinkled my bed
with myrrh, aloes and cinnamon.

18Come, let us drink our fill of love until morning;
let us delight ourselves with caresses.

19For the man is not at home;
he has gone on a long journey.

20He took a bag of money with him;
he will come home at the full moon."

21With her many persuasions she turns him aside;
with her smooth lips she compels him.

22All at once he follows her,
as an ox goes to the slaughter,
or as a fool to the stocks for discipline,

23until an arrow pierces his liver —
as a bird rushes into a snare;
he does not know it will cost him his life.

24Now then, sons, listen to me,
and pay attention to the words of my mouth.

25Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways;
do not stray into her paths;

26for many are the victims she has brought down,
and numerous are all whom she has slain.

27Her house is the way to Sheol,
going down to the chambers of death.

Notes

  • v2 "as the apple of your eye" — ishon, "the little man" of the eye, the pupil, as in Deuteronomy 32:10 and Psalm 17:8.

  • v5 — the same words as 2:16, and the English there is followed.

  • v9 "in the black of night" — be'ishon laylah, "in the pupil of the night," the same word as v2: the darkest point.

  • v14 "I had peace offerings to make; today I have paid my vows" — the meat of a peace offering had to be eaten within a day or two (Leviticus 7:16); she has a feast at home and an empty house.

  • v19 "For the man is not at home" — she does not say "my husband," only "the man."

  • v22 "or as a fool to the stocks for discipline" — the Hebrew is obscure, ukhe'ekhes el musar evil; ekhes is an anklet or fetter (Isaiah 3:18). The Greek reads "as a dog to bonds."

  • vv26–27 — the end of the young man of v7, and the end of the warning that began in 2:16–19.

chapters.title: Wisdom Calls
chapters.html:
Proverbs 8

1Does not wisdom call,
and understanding raise her voice?

2On the top of the heights beside the way,
where the paths meet, she takes her stand;

3beside the gates at the entrance of the city,
at the entry of the doors, she cries aloud:

4"To you, men, I call,
and my voice is to the children of man.

5You simple ones, learn shrewdness;
you fools, learn sense.

6Listen, for I speak noble things,
and from the opening of my lips come right things,

7for my mouth utters truth;
wickedness is detestable to my lips.

8All the words of my mouth are in righteousness;
there is nothing twisted or crooked in them.

9They are all straight to the one who understands,
and right to those who find knowledge.

10Take my discipline instead of silver,
and knowledge rather than choice gold,

11for wisdom is better than jewels,
and nothing desirable can compare with her.

12I, wisdom, dwell with shrewdness,
and I find knowledge and discretion.

13The fear of the LORD is to hate evil.
Pride and arrogance and the way of evil
and the perverse mouth I hate.

14Counsel and sound wisdom are mine;
I am understanding; strength is mine.

15By me kings reign,
and rulers decree what is just;

16by me princes rule,
and nobles, all who judge rightly.

17I love those who love me,
and those who seek me diligently find me.

18Riches and honor are with me,
enduring wealth and righteousness.

19My fruit is better than gold, even fine gold,
and my yield than choice silver.

20I walk in the way of righteousness,
in the paths of justice,

21granting wealth to those who love me
and filling their treasuries.

22The LORD got me at the beginning of His way,
before His works of old.

23From everlasting I was set up,
from the beginning, before the earth was.

24When there were no deeps I was brought forth,
when there were no springs heavy with water.

25Before the mountains had been settled,
before the hills, I was brought forth,

26before He had made the earth or the fields
or the first of the dust of the world.

27When He established the heavens, I was there;
when He drew a circle on the face of the deep,

28when He made firm the skies above,
when the springs of the deep grew strong,

29when He assigned to the sea its limit,
so that the waters would not pass beyond His command,
when He marked out the foundations of the earth,

30then I was beside Him as a master workman,
and I was His delight day by day,
rejoicing before Him always,

31rejoicing in His inhabited world
and delighting in the children of man.

32Now then, sons, listen to me:
blessed are those who keep my ways.

33Hear discipline and be wise,
and do not ignore it.

34Blessed is the one who listens to me,
watching daily at my gates,
waiting beside my doorposts.

35For whoever finds me finds life
and obtains favor from the LORD;

36but whoever misses me harms his own soul;
all who hate me love death."

Notes

  • vv1–3 — Wisdom calls again in the open places, as in 1:20–21, now not in rebuke but in invitation.

  • v11 — nearly the same as 3:15; here "nothing desirable" (chafatsim) for "nothing you desire."

  • v16 "all who judge rightly" — many Hebrew manuscripts and the Greek read "all the judges of the earth."

  • v17 "I love those who love me" — the read form; the written form has "those who love her."

  • v22 "The LORD got me" — qanani, the verb of Genesis 4:1, I have gotten a man, and 14:19, getter of heaven and earth. It can mean acquire, possess, or bring into being; the Greek reads "created me," and the early church argued over the verse. The New Testament speaks of Christ in these terms: the firstborn of all creation… in Him all things were created (Colossians 1:15–17; John 1:1–3).

  • v23 "I was set up" — nissakhti, the verb of Psalm 2:6, I have set My king; some read "I was woven."

  • v30 "as a master workman" — amon; others read amun, "as a little child," or "faithfully." Either way Wisdom was with God at creation, delighting.

  • v36 "whoever misses me" — chote'i, "whoever sins against me," the root meaning "to miss the mark."

chapters.title: Wisdom Has Built Her House
chapters.html:
Proverbs 9

1Wisdom has built her house;
she has hewn her seven pillars.

2She has slaughtered her animals; she has mixed her wine;
she has also set her table.

3She has sent out her young women;
she calls from the highest places in the city:

4"Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!"
To the one who lacks sense she says,

5"Come, eat of my bread
and drink of the wine I have mixed.

6Leave the simple ones, and live,
and walk in the way of understanding."

7Whoever corrects a scoffer gets disgrace for himself,
and whoever reproves a wicked man gets a blemish.

8Do not reprove a scoffer, or he will hate you;
reprove a wise man, and he will love you.

9Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be still wiser;
teach a righteous man, and he will increase in learning.

10The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom,
and the knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.

11For by me your days will be multiplied,
and years of life will be added to you.

12If you are wise, you are wise for yourself;
if you scoff, you alone will bear it.

13The woman Folly is loud;
she is simple and knows nothing.

14She sits at the door of her house,
on a seat at the highest places of the city,

15calling to those who pass by,
who are going straight on their way:

16"Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!"
To the one who lacks sense she says,

17"Stolen water is sweet,
and bread eaten in secret is pleasant."

18But he does not know that the shades are there,
that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.

Notes

  • vv1–6 and 13–18 — two hostesses, Wisdom and Folly, each calling from the high places of the city, each with the same words to the simple (vv4, 16); the first offers life, the second a meal among the dead.

  • v1 "her seven pillars" — a large and finished house; seven is the number of completeness.

  • v6 "Leave the simple ones" — petayim; or "leave simpleness."

  • v7 "gets a blemish" — mumo, the word for a blemish on a sacrifice (Leviticus 22:20); the scoffer's insult sticks to the one who corrected him.

  • v10 "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom" — as in Psalm 111:10; 1:7 has "knowledge." "The Holy One" is plural in Hebrew, qedoshim, a plural of majesty (30:3).

  • v17 "Stolen water is sweet" — the pleasure of what is forbidden (5:15–20; Genesis 3:6).

  • v18 "the shades" — refa'im, as in 2:18. The Greek adds several lines after vv12 and 18 that are not in the Hebrew.

chapters.title: The Memory of the Righteous Is a Blessing
chapters.html:
Proverbs 10

The proverbs of Solomon.

1A wise son makes a glad father,
but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.

2Treasures gained by wickedness do not profit,
but righteousness delivers from death.

3The LORD does not let the righteous go hungry,
but He thrusts away the craving of the wicked.

4A slack hand causes poverty,
but the hand of the diligent makes rich.

5He who gathers in summer is a prudent son;
he who sleeps in harvest is a son who brings shame.

6Blessings are on the head of the righteous,
but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.

7The memory of the righteous is a blessing,
but the name of the wicked will rot.

8The wise of heart will receive commandments,
but a babbling fool will come to ruin.

9Whoever walks in integrity walks securely,
but whoever makes his ways crooked will be found out.

10Whoever winks the eye causes trouble,
and a babbling fool will come to ruin.

11The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life,
but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.

12Hatred stirs up strife,
but love covers all offenses.

13On the lips of the one who understands, wisdom is found,
but a rod is for the back of one who lacks sense.

14The wise store up knowledge,
but the mouth of a fool brings ruin near.

15The rich man's wealth is his strong city;
the ruin of the poor is their poverty.

16The wage of the righteous leads to life,
the gain of the wicked to sin.

17Whoever heeds discipline is on the path to life,
but whoever forsakes reproof leads others astray.

18Whoever conceals hatred has lying lips,
and whoever spreads slander is a fool.

19When words are many, transgression is not lacking,
but whoever restrains his lips is prudent.

20The tongue of the righteous is choice silver;
the heart of the wicked is of little worth.

21The lips of the righteous feed many,
but fools die for lack of sense.

22The blessing of the LORD makes rich,
and He adds no sorrow with it.

23Doing wickedness is like sport to a fool,
and so is wisdom to a man of understanding.

24What the wicked man dreads will come upon him,
but the desire of the righteous will be granted.

25When the whirlwind passes, the wicked is no more,
but the righteous is an everlasting foundation.

26Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes,
so is the sluggard to those who send him.

27The fear of the LORD prolongs days,
but the years of the wicked will be short.

28The hope of the righteous is joy,
but the expectation of the wicked will perish.

29The way of the LORD is a stronghold to the one of integrity,
but ruin to evildoers.

30The righteous will never be moved,
but the wicked will not dwell in the land.

31The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom,
but the perverse tongue will be cut off.

32The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable,
but the mouth of the wicked, what is perverse.

Notes

  • v1 "The proverbs of Solomon" — a new heading: from here to 22:16 the book is a collection of single sayings, most of two lines, the second contrasting with the first.

  • vv6, 11 and 8, 10 — the second lines repeat: "the mouth of the wicked conceals violence" and "a babbling fool will come to ruin" (evil sefatayim, "a fool of lips"). The English keeps them identical.

  • v7 "The memory of the righteous is a blessing" — the words Jewish tradition still says of the dead.

  • v12 "love covers all offenses" — James 5:20 and 1 Peter 4:8 take it up: love covers a multitude of sins.

  • v15 "The rich man's wealth is his strong city" — an observation, not an approval; 18:10–11 sets it beside the name of the LORD is a strong tower.

  • v26 "Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes" — the irritation of a lazy messenger (13:17; 25:13).

  • v29 "to the one of integrity" — tom, integrity, from the same root as tamim, "blameless."

1A false balance is detestable to the LORD,
but a full weight is His delight.

2When pride comes, then comes disgrace,
but with the humble is wisdom.

3The integrity of the upright guides them,
but the crookedness of the treacherous destroys them.

4Wealth does not profit in the day of wrath,
but righteousness delivers from death.

5The righteousness of the blameless keeps his way straight,
but the wicked falls by his own wickedness.

6The righteousness of the upright delivers them,
but the treacherous are caught by their own craving.

7When a wicked man dies, his hope perishes,
and the expectation of wealth perishes.

8The righteous is rescued from trouble,
and the wicked comes into it in his place.

9With his mouth the godless man destroys his neighbor,
but by knowledge the righteous are delivered.

10When it goes well with the righteous, the city rejoices,
and when the wicked perish there are shouts of joy.

11By the blessing of the upright a city is exalted,
but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.

12Whoever despises his neighbor lacks sense,
but a man of understanding keeps silent.

13Whoever goes about as a slanderer reveals secrets,
but the one who is trustworthy in spirit keeps a thing hidden.

14Where there is no guidance a people falls,
but in an abundance of counselors there is victory.

15Whoever puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer harm,
but whoever hates striking hands in pledge is secure.

16A gracious woman gets honor,
and ruthless men get riches.

17A man of loyal love does good to himself,
but a cruel man hurts his own flesh.

18The wicked earns deceptive wages,
but one who sows righteousness gets a true reward.

19As righteousness leads to life,
so whoever pursues evil goes to his death.

20Those of crooked heart are detestable to the LORD,
but those blameless in their way are His delight.

21Be assured, the evil man will not go unpunished,
but the offspring of the righteous will be delivered.

22Like a gold ring in a pig's snout
is a beautiful woman without discretion.

23The desire of the righteous ends only in good;
the expectation of the wicked, in wrath.

24One gives freely, yet grows all the richer;
another withholds what he should give, and only suffers want.

25Whoever brings blessing will be made rich,
and one who waters will himself be watered.

26The people curse him who holds back grain,
but a blessing is on the head of him who sells it.

27Whoever diligently seeks good seeks favor,
but evil comes to him who searches for it.

28Whoever trusts in his riches will fall,
but the righteous will flourish like a green leaf.

29Whoever troubles his own household will inherit the wind,
and the fool will be servant to the wise of heart.

30The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life,
and whoever wins souls is wise.

31If the righteous is repaid on earth,
how much more the wicked and the sinner!

  • v1 "A false balance… a full weight" — honest scales and stones (Leviticus 19:35–36; Deuteronomy 25:13–16); to'evah, "detestable."

  • v3 "destroys them" — the read form; the written form is a spelling variant.

  • v4 — the second line is the same as 10:2b.

  • v7 "the expectation of wealth" — onim, "wealth" or "strength"; others read "the expectation of the wicked."

  • v15 "striking hands in pledge" — the handshake of 6:1.

  • v16 — the Greek has two further lines here, not in the Hebrew.

  • v22 "Like a gold ring in a pig's snout" — beauty without ta'am, "taste," good judgment, is wasted.

  • v30 "whoever wins souls is wise" — loqeach nefashot, "takes lives," here in the good sense of drawing others to life; the Greek reads "the lives of the lawless are cut off."

  • v31 — 1 Peter 4:18 quotes the Greek: If the righteous is scarcely saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?

chapters.title: Lying Lips Are Detestable to the LORD
chapters.html:
Proverbs 12

1Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge,
but whoever hates reproof is stupid.

2A good man obtains favor from the LORD,
but a man of evil devices He condemns.

3No one is established by wickedness,
but the root of the righteous will never be moved.

4A capable wife is her husband's crown,
but she who brings shame is like rot in his bones.

5The thoughts of the righteous are just;
the counsels of the wicked are deceit.

6The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood,
but the mouth of the upright delivers them.

7The wicked are overthrown and are no more,
but the house of the righteous will stand.

8A man is praised according to his good sense,
but one of twisted heart is despised.

9Better to be lowly and have a servant
than to play the great man and lack bread.

10The righteous knows the life of his animal,
but the compassion of the wicked is cruel.

11Whoever works his land will have plenty of bread,
but whoever pursues worthless things lacks sense.

12The wicked covets the catch of evil men,
but the root of the righteous yields fruit.

13In the transgression of the lips is an evil snare,
but the righteous comes out of trouble.

14From the fruit of his mouth a man is satisfied with good,
and the work of a man's hands He repays to him.

15The way of a fool is right in his own eyes,
but a wise man listens to advice.

16A fool's vexation is known at once,
but the shrewd conceals an insult.

17Whoever breathes out truth declares what is right,
but a false witness, deceit.

18There is one whose rash words are like sword thrusts,
but the tongue of the wise brings healing.

19Truthful lips endure forever,
but a lying tongue is but for a moment.

20Deceit is in the heart of those who devise evil,
but those who plan peace have joy.

21No harm befalls the righteous,
but the wicked are filled with trouble.

22Lying lips are detestable to the LORD,
but those who act faithfully are His delight.

23A shrewd man conceals knowledge,
but the heart of fools proclaims folly.

24The hand of the diligent will rule,
while the slack hand will be put to forced labor.

25Anxiety in a man's heart weighs him down,
but a good word makes him glad.

26The righteous guides his neighbor,
but the way of the wicked leads them astray.

27The slack man does not roast his game,
but the diligent man gets precious wealth.

28In the path of righteousness is life,
and in its pathway there is no death.

Notes

  • v1 "is stupid" — ba'ar, brutish, like a beast without reason (30:2; Psalm 73:22); a third word beside evil and kesil.

  • v4 "A capable wife" — eshet chayil, the phrase of 31:10 and Ruth 3:11; chayil is strength, worth, ability.

  • v10 "The righteous knows the life of his animal" — he cares for its needs (Deuteronomy 25:4).

  • v14 "He repays to him" — the read form yashiv, God repays; the written form yashuv, "comes back to him."

  • v17 "Whoever breathes out truth" — yafiach, the verb of 6:19, a false witness who breathes out lies.

  • v26 "The righteous guides his neighbor" — the Hebrew is uncertain; "the righteous searches out his pasture" is another reading.

  • v27 "The slack man does not roast his game" — too lazy even to cook what he caught; charakh occurs only here.

  • v28 "in its pathway there is no death" — al mavet, "not death"; some read el mavet, "to death," and the Greek has "the ways of those who remember evil lead to death."

chapters.title: Hope Deferred Makes the Heart Sick
chapters.html:
Proverbs 13

1A wise son hears his father's discipline,
but a scoffer does not listen to rebuke.

2From the fruit of his mouth a man eats good,
but the desire of the treacherous is violence.

3Whoever guards his mouth preserves his life;
whoever opens wide his lips comes to ruin.

4The soul of the sluggard craves and gets nothing,
but the soul of the diligent is richly supplied.

5The righteous hates a lying word,
but the wicked brings shame and disgrace.

6Righteousness guards the one whose way is blameless,
but wickedness overthrows the sinner.

7One pretends to be rich, yet has nothing;
another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth.

8The ransom of a man's life is his wealth,
but the poor man hears no threat.

9The light of the righteous rejoices,
but the lamp of the wicked will be put out.

10By insolence comes only strife,
but with those who take advice is wisdom.

11Wealth gained from nothing will dwindle,
but whoever gathers little by little will increase it.

12Hope deferred makes the heart sick,
but a desire fulfilled is a tree of life.

13Whoever despises the word brings ruin on himself,
but whoever fears the commandment will be rewarded.

14The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life,
to turn away from the snares of death.

15Good sense wins favor,
but the way of the treacherous is hard.

16Every shrewd man acts with knowledge,
but a fool flaunts folly.

17A wicked messenger falls into trouble,
but a faithful envoy brings healing.

18Poverty and disgrace come to him who ignores discipline,
but whoever heeds reproof is honored.

19A desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul,
but to turn away from evil is detestable to fools.

20Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise,
but the companion of fools suffers harm.

21Disaster pursues sinners,
but the righteous are repaid with good.

22A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children,
but the sinner's wealth is laid up for the righteous.

23The fallow ground of the poor yields much food,
but it is swept away through injustice.

24Whoever spares his rod hates his son,
but whoever loves him disciplines him early.

25The righteous eats to the satisfying of his soul,
but the belly of the wicked suffers want.

Notes

  • v1 "A wise son hears his father's discipline" — the Hebrew has no verb in the first line, "A wise son — a father's discipline"; "hears" comes from the second line.

  • v8 "the poor man hears no threat" — the rich man must pay to save his life; the poor man has nothing anyone would threaten him for.

  • v11 "Wealth gained from nothing" — mehevel, "from a breath," wealth with nothing behind it; the Greek reads "gained hastily with lawlessness."

  • vv12, 19 "a desire fulfilled" — the same phrase twice: in v12 it is a tree of life, in v19 sweet to the soul.

  • v14 — the second line is the same as 14:27b.

  • v15 "the way of the treacherous is hard" — eitan, enduring or hard; the Greek reads "is in ruin."

  • v20 "Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise" — the read forms; the written forms say "Walk with the wise and be wise."

  • v23 "The fallow ground of the poor yields much food" — the poor man's land could feed him, if injustice did not take it.

  • v24 "Whoever spares his rod hates his son" — the rod of correction (22:15; 23:13–14; Hebrews 12:7–11); "early" may mean "diligently."

chapters.title: There Is a Way That Seems Right to a Man
chapters.html:
Proverbs 14

1The wisest of women builds her house,
but folly with her own hands tears it down.

2Whoever walks in uprightness fears the LORD,
but whoever is devious in his ways despises Him.

3In the mouth of a fool is a rod of pride,
but the lips of the wise will preserve them.

4Where there are no oxen, the manger is clean,
but abundant crops come by the strength of the ox.

5A faithful witness does not lie,
but a false witness breathes out lies.

6A scoffer seeks wisdom and finds none,
but knowledge is easy for the one who understands.

7Leave the presence of a fool,
for there you do not meet words of knowledge.

8The wisdom of the shrewd is to understand his way,
but the folly of fools is deceit.

9Fools mock at guilt,
but among the upright there is favor.

10The heart knows its own bitterness,
and no stranger shares its joy.

11The house of the wicked will be destroyed,
but the tent of the upright will flourish.

12There is a way that seems right to a man,
but its end is the ways of death.

13Even in laughter the heart may ache,
and the end of joy may be grief.

14The backslider in heart will be filled with the fruit of his ways,
and a good man with the fruit of his deeds.

15The simple believes everything,
but the shrewd considers his steps.

16A wise man fears and turns away from evil,
but a fool is reckless and careless.

17A man quick to anger acts foolishly,
and a man of evil devices is hated.

18The simple inherit folly,
but the shrewd are crowned with knowledge.

19The evil bow down before the good,
and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.

20The poor man is hated even by his neighbor,
but the rich has many friends.

21Whoever despises his neighbor sins,
but blessed is he who is gracious to the humble.

22Do not those who devise evil go astray?
But loyal love and truth are for those who devise good.

23In all toil there is profit,
but mere talk leads only to want.

24The crown of the wise is their wealth,
but the folly of fools is folly.

25A truthful witness saves lives,
but one who breathes out lies is deceitful.

26In the fear of the LORD there is strong confidence,
and His children will have a refuge.

27The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life,
to turn away from the snares of death.

28In a multitude of people is a king's glory,
but without people a prince is ruined.

29Whoever is slow to anger has great understanding,
but whoever is quick-tempered exalts folly.

30A tranquil heart is life to the body,
but envy is rot to the bones.

31Whoever oppresses the poor insults his Maker,
but whoever is gracious to the needy honors Him.

32The wicked is thrust down by his own evil,
but the righteous has a refuge in his death.

33Wisdom rests in the heart of the one who understands,
but among fools it makes itself known.

34Righteousness exalts a nation,
but sin is a reproach to any people.

35The king's favor is toward a servant who acts wisely,
but his wrath falls on one who acts shamefully.

Notes

  • v1 "The wisest of women builds her house" — as Wisdom built hers (9:1); chokhmot nashim, "the wise ones among women."

  • v3 "a rod of pride" — choter ga'avah: his proud talk is a shoot that grows into a rod for his own back.

  • v5 — the second line is the same as 6:19a, "a false witness who breathes out lies."

  • v12 "There is a way that seems right to a man" — the same words as 16:25, and the English is kept identical.

  • v14 "The backslider in heart" — sug lev, one whose heart turns away.

  • v17 "a man of evil devices" — mezimmot, the word that is "discretion" in 1:4; here in its bad sense, as in 12:2.

  • v21 "gracious to the humble" — the read form anavim; the written form aniyyim, "afflicted," as in 3:34.

  • v27 — the same words as 13:14 with "the fear of the LORD" in place of "the teaching of the wise."

  • v32 "the righteous has a refuge in his death" — the Greek reads "in his integrity," from a reordering of two letters.

  • v34 "sin is a reproach" — chesed, here in its rare second meaning, "shame," as in Leviticus 20:17.

chapters.title: A Soft Answer Turns Away Wrath
chapters.html:
Proverbs 15

1A soft answer turns away wrath,
but a harsh word stirs up anger.

2The tongue of the wise commends knowledge,
but the mouth of fools pours out folly.

3The eyes of the LORD are in every place,
keeping watch on the evil and the good.

4A healing tongue is a tree of life,
but perverseness in it breaks the spirit.

5A fool despises his father's discipline,
but whoever heeds reproof is shrewd.

6In the house of the righteous there is much treasure,
but trouble comes with the income of the wicked.

7The lips of the wise spread knowledge;
not so the heart of fools.

8The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD,
but the prayer of the upright is His delight.

9The way of the wicked is detestable to the LORD,
but He loves him who pursues righteousness.

10There is severe discipline for him who forsakes the way;
whoever hates reproof will die.

11Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD;
how much more the hearts of the children of man!

12A scoffer does not love one who reproves him;
he will not go to the wise.

13A glad heart makes a cheerful face,
but by sorrow of heart the spirit is crushed.

14The heart of the one who understands seeks knowledge,
but the mouth of fools feeds on folly.

15All the days of the afflicted are evil,
but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.

16Better is a little with the fear of the LORD
than great treasure and turmoil with it.

17Better is a dinner of vegetables where love is
than a fattened ox and hatred with it.

18A hot-tempered man stirs up strife,
but he who is slow to anger quiets contention.

19The way of a sluggard is like a hedge of thorns,
but the path of the upright is a level highway.

20A wise son makes a glad father,
but a foolish man despises his mother.

21Folly is joy to one who lacks sense,
but a man of understanding walks straight.

22Plans fail for lack of counsel,
but with many counselors they succeed.

23A man has joy in an apt answer,
and a word in season, how good it is!

24The path of life leads upward for the prudent,
to turn him away from Sheol beneath.

25The LORD tears down the house of the proud
but establishes the widow's boundary.

26Evil thoughts are detestable to the LORD,
but gracious words are pure.

27Whoever is greedy for gain troubles his own household,
but he who hates bribes will live.

28The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer,
but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil things.

29The LORD is far from the wicked,
but He hears the prayer of the righteous.

30The light of the eyes rejoices the heart,
and good news refreshes the bones.

31The ear that listens to life-giving reproof
will dwell among the wise.

32Whoever ignores discipline despises himself,
but he who heeds reproof gains sense.

33The fear of the LORD is the discipline of wisdom,
and humility comes before honor.

Notes

  • v1 "A soft answer turns away wrath" — gentleness disarms anger (25:15; Judges 8:1–3).

  • v3 "The eyes of the LORD are in every place" — as in 2 Chronicles 16:9 and Psalm 33:13–15.

  • vv8–9 — the sacrifice and the way of the wicked are both to'evah; God looks at the heart behind the offering (21:27; 1 Samuel 15:22; Isaiah 1:11–17).

  • v11 "Sheol and Abaddon" — the world of the dead, as in Job 26:6; if they lie open to God, how much more a human heart.

  • v14 "the mouth of fools" — the read form pi; the written form penei, "the face of fools."

  • v20 — the first line is the same as 10:1.

  • v25 "establishes the widow's boundary" — the boundary stones of the defenseless, which the powerful moved (22:28; 23:10–11; Deuteronomy 19:14).

  • v33 "humility comes before honor" — repeated at 18:12.

Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD; how much more the hearts of the children of man!
A scoffer does not love one who reproves him; he will not go to the wise.
A glad heart makes a cheerful face, but by sorrow of heart the spirit is crushed.

chapters.title: The LORD Establishes His Steps
chapters.html:
Proverbs 16

1The plans of the heart belong to man,
but the answer of the tongue is from the LORD.

2All the ways of a man are pure in his own eyes,
but the LORD weighs the spirits.

3Commit your works to the LORD,
and your plans will be established.

4The LORD has made everything for its purpose,
even the wicked for the day of evil.

5Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD;
be assured, he will not go unpunished.

6By loyal love and truth iniquity is atoned for,
and by the fear of the LORD one turns away from evil.

7When a man's ways please the LORD,
He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.

8Better is a little with righteousness
than great income with injustice.

9The heart of man plans his way,
but the LORD establishes his steps.

10An oracle is on the lips of a king;
his mouth does not sin in judgment.

11A just balance and scales are the LORD's;
all the weights in the bag are His work.

12It is detestable to kings to do wickedness,
for a throne is established by righteousness.

13Righteous lips are the delight of kings,
and they love him who speaks what is right.

14A king's wrath is a messenger of death,
and a wise man will appease it.

15In the light of a king's face is life,
and his favor is like the clouds of the spring rain.

16How much better to get wisdom than gold!
To get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver.

17The highway of the upright turns away from evil;
whoever guards his way preserves his life.

18Pride goes before destruction,
and a haughty spirit before a fall.

19Better to be of a lowly spirit with the humble
than to divide the spoil with the proud.

20Whoever gives thought to the word will find good,
and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD.

21The wise of heart is called understanding,
and sweetness of speech increases learning.

22Good sense is a fountain of life to those who have it,
but the discipline of fools is folly.

23The heart of the wise makes his mouth prudent
and adds learning to his lips.

24Gracious words are a honeycomb,
sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.

25There is a way that seems right to a man,
but its end is the ways of death.

26A worker's appetite works for him,
for his mouth urges him on.

27A worthless man digs up evil,
and on his lips it is like a scorching fire.

28A perverse man spreads strife,
and a whisperer separates close friends.

29A man of violence entices his neighbor
and leads him in a way that is not good.

30Whoever winks his eyes plans perverse things;
whoever purses his lips brings evil to pass.

31Gray hair is a crown of glory;
it is gained in the way of righteousness.

32Better is one slow to anger than the mighty,
and one who rules his spirit than one who takes a city.

33The lot is cast into the lap,
but its every decision is from the LORD.

Notes

  • vv1–9 — man plans, and the LORD decides (19:21; 20:24); the theme returns in the last verse (v33).

  • v3 "Commit your works to the LORD" — gol, "roll" them onto Him (Psalm 22:8; 37:5).

  • v5 "be assured" — yad leyad, "hand to hand," as in 11:21, and the English there is followed.

  • v6 "By loyal love and truth iniquity is atoned for" — chesed and emet, the pair of 3:3.

  • v10 "An oracle is on the lips of a king" — qesem, elsewhere divination (Deuteronomy 18:10); here the king's word as decisive as an oracle.

  • v14 "a messenger of death" — mal'akhei mavet, plural, "messengers of death."

  • v19 "with the humble" — the read form, as in 14:21.

  • v25 — the same words as 14:12.

  • v27 "on his lips" — the read form is singular, "lip"; the written form plural.

  • v33 "The lot is cast into the lap" — the lot, as with the Urim (Numbers 27:21) or in dividing the land (Joshua 18:6); the outcome is the LORD's (Acts 1:26).

chapters.title: A Friend Loves at All Times
chapters.html:
Proverbs 17

1Better is a dry morsel with quiet
than a house full of feasting with strife.

2A servant who acts wisely will rule over a son who brings shame
and will share the inheritance among the brothers.

3The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold,
but the LORD tests hearts.

4An evildoer listens to wicked lips,
and a liar gives ear to a destructive tongue.

5Whoever mocks the poor insults his Maker;
whoever rejoices at calamity will not go unpunished.

6Grandchildren are the crown of the aged,
and the glory of children is their fathers.

7Fine speech is not fitting for a fool,
still less lying speech for a noble.

8A bribe is a charm in the eyes of the one who gives it;
wherever he turns, he prospers.

9Whoever covers an offense seeks love,
but whoever repeats a matter separates close friends.

10A rebuke goes deeper into one who understands
than a hundred blows into a fool.

11An evil man seeks only rebellion,
and a cruel messenger will be sent against him.

12Let a man meet a bear robbed of her cubs
rather than a fool in his folly.

13If anyone returns evil for good,
evil will not depart from his house.

14The beginning of strife is like letting out water,
so quit before the quarrel breaks out.

15Whoever justifies the wicked and whoever condemns the righteous —
both alike are detestable to the LORD.

16Why should a fool have money in his hand to buy wisdom,
when he has no sense?

17A friend loves at all times,
and a brother is born for adversity.

18A man lacking sense strikes hands in pledge
and puts up security in the presence of his neighbor.

19Whoever loves transgression loves strife;
whoever makes his door high seeks destruction.

20One with a crooked heart finds no good,
and one with a perverse tongue falls into evil.

21He who fathers a fool has grief,
and the father of a fool has no joy.

22A glad heart is good medicine,
but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.

23The wicked takes a bribe from the bosom
to pervert the paths of justice.

24Wisdom is before the face of the one who understands,
but the eyes of a fool are on the ends of the earth.

25A foolish son is a grief to his father
and bitterness to her who bore him.

26To punish the righteous is not good,
nor to strike the noble for their uprightness.

27Whoever restrains his words has knowledge,
and one who is cool in spirit is a man of understanding.

28Even a fool who keeps silent is considered wise;
when he closes his lips, he is counted as understanding.

Notes

  • v3 "The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold" — repeated at 27:21; God tests the heart as fire tests metal (Psalm 66:10; Malachi 3:3).

  • v5 "Whoever mocks the poor insults his Maker" — as in 14:31.

  • vv7, 21 "a fool" — here naval, the man without reverence, as in Psalm 14:1, and the English there is followed; v7 "still less" (af ki) is the form of 19:10.

  • v8 "A bribe is a charm in the eyes of the one who gives it" — an observation of how bribes work, not approval; v23 condemns them.

  • v13 "evil will not depart" — the read form; the written form is a spelling variant.

  • v15 — the second line, "both alike are detestable to the LORD," returns at 20:10.

  • v19 "whoever makes his door high" — a proud display of wealth, or a high gate that invites robbers; some read "his mouth."

  • v27 "one who is cool in spirit" — the read form yeqar ruach, "cool," or "precious," of spirit; the written form has veqar ruach, "and cool of spirit."

chapters.title: The Name of the LORD Is a Strong Tower
chapters.html:
Proverbs 18

1Whoever isolates himself seeks his own desire;
he breaks out against all sound wisdom.

2A fool takes no pleasure in understanding,
but only in laying bare his own heart.

3When the wicked man comes, contempt comes also,
and with dishonor comes reproach.

4The words of a man's mouth are deep waters;
the fountain of wisdom is a gushing stream.

5It is not good to show favor to the wicked,
to turn aside the righteous in judgment.

6A fool's lips walk into a quarrel,
and his mouth invites a beating.

7A fool's mouth is his ruin,
and his lips are a snare to his soul.

8The words of a whisperer are like delicious morsels;
they go down into the inner parts of the body.

9Whoever is slack in his work
is a brother to him who destroys.

10The name of the LORD is a strong tower;
the righteous runs into it and is safe.

11The rich man's wealth is his strong city,
and like a high wall in his imagination.

12Before destruction a man's heart is haughty,
but humility comes before honor.

13If one gives an answer before he hears,
it is his folly and shame.

14A man's spirit will endure sickness,
but a crushed spirit, who can bear?

15An understanding heart acquires knowledge,
and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.

16A man's gift makes room for him
and brings him before the great.

17The one who states his case first seems right,
until his neighbor comes and examines him.

18The lot puts an end to quarrels
and decides between the powerful.

19A brother offended is harder to win than a strong city,
and quarrels are like the bars of a fortress.

20From the fruit of a man's mouth his stomach is satisfied;
he is satisfied by the yield of his lips.

21Death and life are in the power of the tongue,
and those who love it will eat its fruit.

22He who finds a wife finds a good thing
and obtains favor from the LORD.

23The poor man pleads for mercy,
but the rich man answers roughly.

24A man of many companions may come to ruin,
but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

Notes

  • v1 "Whoever isolates himself" — the one who cuts himself off from others to follow his own will; the line is hard, and the Greek reads it differently.

  • v8 "like delicious morsels" — mitlahamim occurs only here and in 26:22, where the verse is repeated.

  • vv10–11 — set side by side: the righteous runs into the name of the LORD, the rich man trusts the strong city of his wealth (10:15a, and the English there is followed) — "in his imagination."

  • v12 — the second line is the same as 15:33b.

  • v17 "until his neighbor comes" — the read form; the written form is a spelling variant.

  • v18 "The lot puts an end to quarrels" — as in 16:33.

  • v19 "quarrels" — the read form midyanim, as in 6:14; the verse is hard, and the Greek reads "A brother helped by a brother is like a strong city."

  • v22 — the second line is the same as 8:35b, "and obtains favor from the LORD."

  • v24 "A man of many companions may come to ruin" — lehitro'ea, to be broken, a play on re'im, "companions."

chapters.title: The Purpose of the LORD Will Stand
chapters.html:
Proverbs 19

1Better is a poor man who walks in his integrity
than one who is crooked in speech and is a fool.

2Desire without knowledge is not good,
and whoever hurries with his feet misses the way.

3A man's folly ruins his way,
and his heart rages against the LORD.

4Wealth adds many friends,
but the poor man is separated from his friend.

5A false witness will not go unpunished,
and one who breathes out lies will not escape.

6Many seek the favor of a noble,
and everyone is a friend to a man who gives gifts.

7All the brothers of a poor man hate him;
how much more do his friends go far from him!
He pursues them with words; words are all he has.

8Whoever gets sense loves his own soul;
whoever keeps understanding will find good.

9A false witness will not go unpunished,
and one who breathes out lies will perish.

10Luxury is not fitting for a fool,
still less for a servant to rule over princes.

11A man's good sense makes him slow to anger,
and it is his glory to overlook an offense.

12A king's wrath is like the roaring of a lion,
but his favor is like dew on the grass.

13A foolish son is ruin to his father,
and a wife's quarreling is a continual dripping.

14House and wealth are an inheritance from fathers,
but a prudent wife is from the LORD.

15Laziness casts into a deep sleep,
and a slack soul will go hungry.

16Whoever keeps the commandment keeps his life;
whoever is careless of his ways will die.

17Whoever is gracious to the poor lends to the LORD,
and He will repay him for his deed.

18Discipline your son while there is hope,
and do not set your heart on putting him to death.

19A man of great wrath will pay the penalty;
for if you rescue him, you will have to do it again.

20Listen to advice and accept discipline,
so that you may be wise in your latter end.

21Many are the plans in a man's heart,
but it is the purpose of the LORD that will stand.

22What is desired in a man is loyal love,
and a poor man is better than a liar.

23The fear of the LORD leads to life,
and whoever has it rests satisfied; he will not be visited by harm.

24The sluggard buries his hand in the dish
and will not even bring it back to his mouth.

25Strike a scoffer, and the simple will learn shrewdness;
reprove one who understands, and he will gain knowledge.

26He who robs his father and drives away his mother
is a son who brings shame and disgrace.

27Cease, my son, to hear discipline,
only to stray from the words of knowledge.

28A worthless witness mocks at justice,
and the mouth of the wicked swallows iniquity.

29Judgments are ready for scoffers,
and beatings for the backs of fools.

Notes

  • vv5, 9 — the same first line, "A false witness will not go unpunished"; the second lines differ, "will not escape" and "will perish."

  • v7 — a three-line saying, rare in this collection. The last line is hard: the read form lo, "to him," gives "words are all he has"; the written form lo, "not," gives "they are not there."

  • v10 — the form of 17:7, "not fitting… still less."

  • v12 — the first line returns at 20:2a.

  • v16 "will die" — the read form yamut; the written form yumat, "will be put to death."

  • v17 "Whoever is gracious to the poor lends to the LORD" — God takes the debt on Himself (Matthew 25:40).

  • v18 "do not set your heart on putting him to death" — do not let discipline become cruelty, or: do not leave him uncorrected to his ruin.

  • v19 "A man of great wrath" — the read form gedal; the written form is unclear.

  • v21 — as in 16:9.

  • v24 "The sluggard buries his hand in the dish" — repeated at 26:15.

chapters.title: The Lamp of the LORD
chapters.html:
Proverbs 20

1Wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler,
and whoever is led astray by it is not wise.

2The terror of a king is like the roaring of a lion;
whoever provokes him sins against his own life.

3It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife,
but every fool will break out.

4The sluggard does not plow in autumn;
he will look for a crop at harvest and have nothing.

5Counsel in a man's heart is like deep water,
but a man of understanding will draw it out.

6Many a man proclaims his own loyal love,
but a faithful man, who can find?

7The righteous who walks in his integrity —
blessed are his children after him!

8A king who sits on the throne of judgment
winnows all evil with his eyes.

9Who can say, "I have made my heart clean;
I am pure from my sin"?

10Unequal weights and unequal measures —
both alike are detestable to the LORD.

11Even a child makes himself known by his acts,
whether his conduct is pure and right.

12The hearing ear and the seeing eye —
the LORD has made them both.

13Do not love sleep, or you will come to poverty;
open your eyes, and you will have plenty of bread.

14"Bad, bad," says the buyer,
but when he has gone his way, then he boasts.

15There is gold and an abundance of jewels,
but the lips of knowledge are a precious vessel.

16Take a man's garment when he has put up security for a stranger,
and hold it in pledge when he puts it up for a foreign woman.

17Bread gained by deceit is sweet to a man,
but afterward his mouth will be filled with gravel.

18Plans are established by counsel;
by wise guidance wage war.

19Whoever goes about as a slanderer reveals secrets;
so do not associate with one who opens his lips wide.

20If one curses his father or his mother,
his lamp will be put out in the black of darkness.

21An inheritance gained hastily in the beginning
will not be blessed in the end.

22Do not say, "I will repay evil";
wait for the LORD, and He will deliver you.

23Unequal weights are detestable to the LORD,
and false scales are not good.

24A man's steps are from the LORD;
how then can man understand his way?

25It is a snare for a man to say rashly, "It is holy,"
and to reflect only after making vows.

26A wise king winnows the wicked
and drives the wheel over them.

27The breath of man is the lamp of the LORD,
searching all the inner parts of the body.

28Loyal love and truth preserve the king,
and by loyal love his throne is upheld.

29The glory of young men is their strength,
and the splendor of old men is their gray hair.

30Blows that wound cleanse away evil;
strokes reach the inner parts of the body.

Notes

  • v1 "Wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler" — lets, "scoffer," as wine makes a man; "led astray" is shagah, the verb of 5:19–23.

  • v4 "in autumn" — choref, the season of the early rains when the fields are plowed; "he will look for a crop" follows the read form.

  • v9 "Who can say, 'I have made my heart clean'?" — no one (1 Kings 8:46; Ecclesiastes 7:20; 1 John 1:8).

  • vv10, 23 "Unequal weights" — literally "a stone and a stone," two sets of weights, one for buying and one for selling (11:1; Deuteronomy 25:13–16).

  • v16 "a foreign woman" — the read form nokhriyyah; the written form nokhrim, "foreigners." Repeated at 27:13.

  • v20 "in the black of darkness" — be'ishon, "in the pupil of darkness," as in 7:9; the read form is a spelling variant. "His lamp will be put out" as in 13:9.

  • v21 "gained hastily" — the read form mevohelet; the written form mevochelet, "gained by greed."

  • v25 "to say rashly, 'It is holy'" — dedicating something to God in haste and regretting the vow after (Ecclesiastes 5:4–6).

It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife, but every fool will break out.

A king who sits on the throne of judgment winnows all evil with his eyes.

chapters.title: The King's Heart Is in the Hand of the LORD
chapters.html:
Proverbs 21

1The king's heart is a stream of water in the hand of the LORD;
He turns it wherever He wishes.

2Every way of a man is right in his own eyes,
but the LORD weighs the hearts.

3To do righteousness and justice
is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.

4Haughty eyes and a proud heart —
the lamp of the wicked — are sin.

5The plans of the diligent lead surely to profit,
but everyone who is hasty comes surely to want.

6Getting treasures by a lying tongue
is a fleeting vapor for those who seek death.

7The violence of the wicked will sweep them away,
because they refuse to do justice.

8The way of the guilty man is crooked,
but the conduct of the pure is right.

9It is better to live in a corner of the housetop
than in a house shared with a quarrelsome wife.

10The soul of the wicked desires evil;
his neighbor finds no favor in his eyes.

11When a scoffer is punished, the simple becomes wise;
when the wise is instructed, he gains knowledge.

12The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked;
He throws the wicked down to ruin.

13Whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor
will himself call out and not be answered.

14A gift in secret averts anger,
and a bribe in the bosom, strong wrath.

15When justice is done, it is a joy to the righteous
but terror to evildoers.

16A man who wanders from the way of good sense
will rest in the assembly of the shades.

17Whoever loves pleasure will be a poor man;
whoever loves wine and oil will not be rich.

18The wicked is a ransom for the righteous,
and the treacherous for the upright.

19It is better to live in a desert land
than with a quarrelsome and fretful wife.

20Precious treasure and oil are in the dwelling of the wise,
but a foolish man devours it.

21Whoever pursues righteousness and loyal love
will find life, righteousness and honor.

22A wise man scales the city of the mighty
and brings down the stronghold in which they trust.

23Whoever guards his mouth and his tongue
guards his soul from trouble.

24"Scoffer" is the name of the arrogant, haughty man
who acts with arrogant fury.

25The desire of the sluggard kills him,
for his hands refuse to work.

26All day long he craves and craves,
but the righteous gives and does not hold back.

27The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable;
how much more when he brings it with evil intent!

28A false witness will perish,
but the man who listens will speak forever.

29A wicked man puts on a bold face,
but the upright gives thought to his way.

30There is no wisdom, no understanding,
no counsel against the LORD.

31The horse is made ready for the day of battle,
but victory belongs to the LORD.

Notes

  • v1 "a stream of water in the hand of the LORD" — like irrigation channels a farmer turns where he wants; even the most powerful heart is in God's hand.

  • v2 "the LORD weighs the hearts" — as in 16:2 ("the spirits") and 24:12.

  • v3 "more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice" — 1 Samuel 15:22; Hosea 6:6; Micah 6:6–8.

  • v4 "the lamp of the wicked" — nir, "lamp," or, with other vowels, "the tilled field," the work of the wicked.

  • v6 "for those who seek death" — the Hebrew is followed; the Greek and some Hebrew manuscripts read "snares of death."

  • vv9, 19 "a quarrelsome wife" — v9 is repeated at 25:24; midyanim, the read form in v19.

  • v12 "The Righteous One" — tsaddiq, here likely God, who sees the house of the wicked and brings it down; some take it as a righteous man.

  • v16 "the assembly of the shades" — refa'im, as in 2:18 and 9:18.

  • v27 — the first line is as in 15:8, without "to the LORD."

  • v29 "the upright gives thought to his way" — the read form yavin darko; the written form yakhin derakhav, "makes his ways firm."

chapters.title: Train Up a Child
chapters.html:
Proverbs 22

1A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches,
and favor is better than silver or gold.

2The rich and the poor meet together;
the LORD is the Maker of them all.

3The shrewd sees evil and hides himself,
but the simple go on and suffer for it.

4The reward for humility and the fear of the LORD
is riches and honor and life.

5Thorns and snares are in the way of the crooked;
whoever guards his soul will keep far from them.

6Train up a child in the way he should go;
even when he is old he will not depart from it.

7The rich rules over the poor,
and the borrower is the servant of the lender.

8Whoever sows injustice will reap trouble,
and the rod of his fury will fail.

9Whoever has a generous eye will be blessed,
for he shares his bread with the poor.

10Drive out the scoffer, and strife will go out,
and quarreling and disgrace will cease.

11Whoever loves purity of heart
and whose speech is gracious will have the king as his friend.

12The eyes of the LORD keep watch over knowledge,
but He overthrows the words of the treacherous.

13The sluggard says, "There is a lion outside!
I shall be killed in the streets!"

14The mouth of strange women is a deep pit;
he with whom the LORD is angry will fall into it.

15Folly is bound up in the heart of a child,
but the rod of discipline drives it far from him.

16Whoever oppresses the poor to increase his own wealth,
or gives to the rich, will only come to want.

17Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise,
and apply your heart to my knowledge;

18for it will be pleasant if you keep them within you,
if all of them are ready on your lips.

19So that your trust may be in the LORD,
I have made them known to you today, even to you.

20Have I not written for you excellent things
of counsel and knowledge,

21to make you know what is right and true,
so that you may give a true answer to those who sent you?

22Do not rob the poor because he is poor,
or crush the afflicted at the gate;

23for the LORD will plead their cause
and rob of life those who rob them.

24Make no friendship with a man given to anger,
and do not go with a hot-tempered man,

25or you will learn his ways
and entangle yourself in a snare.

26Do not be one of those who strike hands in pledge,
who put up security for debts.

27If you have nothing with which to pay,
why should your bed be taken from under you?

28Do not move the ancient boundary stone
that your fathers set up.

29Do you see a man skilled in his work?
He will stand before kings;
he will not stand before obscure men.

Notes

  • v2 "The rich and the poor meet together" — they have one Maker (29:13; Job 31:15).

  • v3 — repeated at 27:12; "hides himself" is the read form.

  • v6 "in the way he should go" — al pi darko, "according to his way," the way fitting for him.

  • v13 "There is a lion outside!" — the sluggard's excuse, repeated at 26:13.

  • v14 "The mouth of strange women" — zarot, as in 2:16.

  • v17 "the words of the wise" — a new collection begins (22:17–24:22), addressed to "you"; much of 22:17–23:11 is close to an Egyptian teaching, the Instruction of Amenemope, in thirty chapters.

  • v20 "excellent things" — the read form shalishim; the written form shilshom, "formerly." Many read sheloshim, "thirty sayings," matching Amenemope's thirty chapters.

  • v23 "for the LORD will plead their cause" — the poor have a defender (23:11).

  • v28 "Do not move the ancient boundary stone" — as in Deuteronomy 19:14; repeated at 23:10.
